message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"ef21b77e197aac30064d8c47a1017e3116373f81a63a6ff9d35ae39096257ac2","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-va-class-std:lineage:74","source_registry_sha256":"b6300aba50e85a8fd509daf2f853e3d2d116b38a9707baf75df5057c8071f937","units":[{"unit_id":"sec07-u01","module_id":"sec07-m01","objective_ids":["sec07-u01"],"title":{"text":"Yielding at intersections","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-R02","sec07-F02"]},"why_how":[{"text":"You always yield to pedestrians at intersections, driveways and parking areas, marked crosswalk or not.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-R02"]},{"text":"Left turns, driveways, uncontrolled crossings, T junctions and signals each have a stated yield rule.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ivy and another driver reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same moment, and the other car is on Ivy's right.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Where uncontrolled roads meet with simultaneous arrivals, you yield to the vehicle on your right.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},"result":{"text":"Ivy yields and lets the car on her right go first.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a plain green light lets a left turn go ahead of oncoming traffic.","fact_ids":["sec07-R01"]},"correction":{"text":"A plain left turn yields to oncoming traffic, while only a green-arrow left turn owns the right-of-way.","fact_ids":["sec07-R01","sec07-F02"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Right goes first; side road yields at a T.","fact_ids":["sec07-R03"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Ivy and another driver arrive together at an uncontrolled intersection, and the other car is on her right. Who goes first?","fact_ids":["sec07-F04"]},"answer":{"text":"The car on Ivy's right; she yields.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},"rationale":{"text":"Simultaneous arrivals at uncontrolled crossings yield to the vehicle on the right, while at a T the side road yields to the through road.","fact_ids":["sec07-R03"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Who goes first","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Pedestrians, always.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},{"text":"Left turns and driveways.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},{"text":"Uncontrolled crossings, T junctions and signals.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on right-of-way at intersections and driveways. Right-of-way rules decide who goes first, and the manual states them plainly. We begin with pedestrians, because you always yield to them at intersections, driveways and parking areas, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked. Then we cover left turns, leaving driveways and parking lots, uncontrolled intersections where two drivers arrive together, T junctions, and yielding at red and green lights. By the end of this lesson you should be able to say who yields in each of these situations. The rules are short, so learn them exactly as the manual states them.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Pedestrians first","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-R02","sec07-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Intersections, driveways, parking areas.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-R02","sec07-F03"]},{"text":"Marked or unmarked crosswalks.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-R02","sec07-F03"]},{"text":"The same yield everywhere.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-R02","sec07-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Always yield to pedestrians at intersections, driveways and parking areas, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked. Marked crosswalks, unmarked crossings, driveways and parking areas all demand the same pedestrian yield. A missing crosswalk does not change the rule. When you leave a driveway, a parking lot or a parking area, you yield to roadway traffic and to pedestrians on the sidewalk. So the pedestrian yield follows you from the intersection to the driveway to the parking lot. Wherever a pedestrian is crossing your path in one of these places, the pedestrian goes first, and you wait until they have crossed.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-R02","sec07-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Left turns","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-R01","sec07-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"A left turn yields to oncoming traffic.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-R01","sec07-F01"]},{"text":"Unless a green arrow grants the turn.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-R01","sec07-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"A left turn yields to oncoming traffic, unless a green arrow grants the turn. Put as a contrast: a plain left turn yields to oncoming traffic, while a green-arrow left turn owns the right-of-way. The difference is the arrow. On a plain green light, you may turn left, but only after oncoming traffic has passed or when it is clear. With a green arrow pointing left, the turn is yours. This rule fits together with the pedestrian rule from the last slide: even when you are turning, any pedestrian crossing your path at the intersection is yielded to. So a left turn on a plain green yields twice, to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-R01","sec07-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":46,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The right-hand rule and the T","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Simultaneous arrivals: yield to the car on your right.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},{"text":"At a T, the side road always yields.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},{"text":"The through road goes first.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap: two rules for uncontrolled intersections that are easy to mix up. Where uncontrolled roads meet and two vehicles arrive at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right. But at a T intersection, the side road always yields to the through road, no matter which side the other car is on. So simultaneous arrivals at bare crossings defer to the right, while T junctions defer to the through road. If you are on the side road at a T, you yield, even if the other car would be on your left. If you are on the through road, the side road yields to you. Ask first whether the junction is a T.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":47,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Yielding at signals","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Red: yield to crossing pedestrians and through traffic.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},{"text":"Green: yield to pedestrians and vehicles still inside.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},{"text":"A green light does not clear the intersection.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Signals have yield rules too. At a red light, yield to crossing pedestrians and to through traffic. On a green light, yield to pedestrians still in the intersection and to vehicles still inside it. So red asks you to yield to crossing pedestrians and through traffic, while green asks you to yield to those still inside the intersection. The green light gives you permission to go, but it does not clear the intersection for you. Anyone who is still in it when your light turns green, on foot or in a vehicle, is yielded to. Once they have cleared, you proceed, still watching for pedestrians as you turn.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the arrival","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Uncontrolled intersection.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},{"text":"You arrive together.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},{"text":"The other car is on your right.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: Ivy and another driver reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same moment, and the other car is on Ivy's right. Who goes first? Work it out before reading on. The answer is the car on Ivy's right. Where uncontrolled roads meet with simultaneous arrivals, you yield to the vehicle on your right. If the junction were a T and Ivy were on the side road, she would yield to the through road no matter which side the other car was on. Ask first whether it is a T, and if not, look to your right. Right goes first, and the side road yields at a T.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Yield rules recap","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Pedestrians: always.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},{"text":"Left turns: unless a green arrow.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},{"text":"Right-hand rule; T: side road yields.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close the lesson: always yield to pedestrians at intersections, driveways and parking areas, marked crosswalk or not. A left turn yields to oncoming traffic unless a green arrow grants the turn. Leaving a driveway or parking lot, yield to roadway traffic and to pedestrians on the sidewalk. At an uncontrolled intersection with simultaneous arrivals, yield to the vehicle on your right, and at a T, the side road always yields to the through road. At a red light, yield to crossing pedestrians and through traffic, and on green, yield to pedestrians and vehicles still inside the intersection. Right goes first, and the side road yields at a T.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec07-u02","module_id":"sec07-m02","objective_ids":["sec07-u02"],"title":{"text":"Emergency vehicles and walk signals","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-R05"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing lights get the road: pull to the edge, stop and wait.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06"]},{"text":"Stopped vehicles with flashers call for the Move Over rule, and pedestrian signals tell walkers when to start and finish.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-F08"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Sara sees a construction vehicle stopped on the shoulder with amber lights flashing.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Move Over for stopped emergency and construction vehicles flashing blue, red or amber by changing lanes away or slowing to a safe speed.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05"]},"result":{"text":"Sara changes lanes away from the vehicle, or slows to a safe speed if she cannot change lanes.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a stopped vehicle with flashers requires the same full stop as an approaching siren.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05"]},"correction":{"text":"Active sirens and lights demand pulling over, stopping and waiting, while stopped flashers demand only a lane move or a safe slowdown.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F06","sec07-F07"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Moving siren: pull over; stopped lights: move over.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Sara passes a construction vehicle stopped on the shoulder with amber lights flashing. What does the Move Over rule ask?","fact_ids":["sec07-F07"]},"answer":{"text":"Change lanes away or slow to a safe speed.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05"]},"rationale":{"text":"Stopped flashers demand a lane move or a safe slowdown, while active sirens demand pulling over and stopping.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Making way","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Sirens and flashing lights.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08"]},{"text":"Funeral processions.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08"]},{"text":"Move Over and walk signals.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on making way for emergency vehicles and reading pedestrian signals. Emergency vehicles that are sounding sirens or flashing lights, and funeral processions, hold the right-of-way. Stopped emergency and construction vehicles with flashing lights are covered by the Move Over rule, which asks something different. And pedestrian signals tell walkers when to start crossing, when to wait, and when to finish. In this lesson we will separate the two emergency rules, which ask for different responses, and then learn the three pedestrian signals as a set: walk, don't-walk, and countdown.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Sirens and processions","fact_ids":["sec07-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Pull to the nearest road edge and stop.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06"]},{"text":"Leave any intersection first.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06"]},{"text":"Wait until they pass; funerals also have right-of-way.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"For emergency vehicles sounding sirens or flashing lights, pull to the nearest road edge and stop. If you are in an intersection, leave it first, then pull over. Wait until the emergency vehicles pass. Funeral processions also hold the right-of-way. The order of steps matters: you do not stop in the middle of an intersection. You clear it, pull to the nearest edge of the road, stop, and wait. Only after the emergency vehicles have passed do you continue. Learn this as a sequence of four steps: leave the intersection, pull to the edge, stop, and wait.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s3","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Moving versus stopped","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Active siren or lights: pull over, stop, wait.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]},{"text":"Stopped with flashers: change lanes away or slow.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]},{"text":"Also for stalled vehicles with flares or flashers.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. The Move Over rule is not the pull-over rule. Move Over applies to stopped emergency and construction vehicles flashing blue, red or amber lights. For them, change lanes away, or slow to a safe speed. Do the same for stalled vehicles showing flares, warning lights or flashers. So active sirens and lights demand pulling over, stopping and waiting, while stopped flashers demand only a lane move or a safe slowdown. If the emergency vehicle is coming toward you or behind you with its siren on, you pull over and stop. If it is already stopped on the shoulder with its lights on, you move over or slow down.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":45,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Pedestrian signals","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-R06","sec07-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Walk: cross.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-R06","sec07-F05"]},{"text":"Don't-walk: wait.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-R06","sec07-F05"]},{"text":"Countdown: finish crossing, do not start.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-R06","sec07-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Pedestrian signals have three messages. Walk means cross. Don't-walk means wait. A countdown means finish crossing without starting. Put as a contrast: walk starts crossings and don't-walk forbids them, while a countdown only lets started crossings finish. As a driver, these signals tell you what the pedestrians around you are allowed to do. A pedestrian who started on walk may still be crossing during the countdown, and you yield to pedestrians still in the intersection when your light turns green. So reading the pedestrian signal helps you know who may still be in the crosswalk as you prepare to go.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-R06","sec07-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check Move Over","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Construction vehicle on the shoulder.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05"]},{"text":"Amber lights flashing.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05"]},{"text":"What does the rule ask?","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: Sara is driving past a construction vehicle stopped on the shoulder with amber lights flashing. What does the Move Over rule ask her to do? Work it out before reading on. The answer: change lanes away from the vehicle, or slow to a safe speed. Move Over applies to stopped emergency and construction vehicles flashing blue, red or amber, and to stalled vehicles showing flares, warning lights or flashers. Sara does not need to pull over and stop, because that is the rule for emergency vehicles with active sirens or flashing lights coming through. Moving siren, pull over; stopped lights, move over.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Making way recap","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Sirens: leave intersection, edge, stop, wait.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-R05"]},{"text":"Stopped flashers: move over or slow.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-R05"]},{"text":"Walk, don't-walk, countdown.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close the lesson: for emergency vehicles sounding sirens or flashing lights, first leave any intersection you are in, then pull to the nearest road edge, stop, and wait until they pass. Funeral processions also hold the right-of-way. For stopped emergency and construction vehicles flashing blue, red or amber, and for stalled vehicles with flares or flashers, change lanes away or slow to a safe speed. Pedestrian signals read walk to cross, don't-walk to wait, and countdown to finish crossing without starting. The memory line for the two emergency rules is: moving siren, pull over; stopped lights, move over.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec07-u03","module_id":"sec07-m03","objective_ids":["sec07-u03"],"title":{"text":"Roundabouts","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-R07"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Entering a roundabout means slowing and yielding to every circulating lane.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09"]},{"text":"Inside, you follow signs and arrows for your lane, exit with a right turn and give trucks extra room.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Noor drives into a two-lane roundabout beside a large truck.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Give trucks extra room for their wider arcs, and do not pass beside them.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},"result":{"text":"Noor drops back and does not drive beside the truck as it circles.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking circulating traffic must yield to cars entering the roundabout.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07"]},"correction":{"text":"Roundabout entry yields to every circulating lane, while circulating means counterclockwise travel, signed lane choice and a right-turn exit.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-F09"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Yield in, circle left, exit right.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Noor is in a roundabout next to a large truck. Should she drive beside it?","fact_ids":["sec07-F10"]},"answer":{"text":"No. Give the truck extra room and do not pass beside it.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},"rationale":{"text":"Cars hold tight signed lanes, while trucks swing wider arcs that forbid driving beside them.","fact_ids":["sec07-R08"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Inside the circle","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Slow and yield on entry.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},{"text":"Counterclockwise travel.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},{"text":"Lanes, exits and trucks.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on roundabouts. A roundabout is a circular intersection with a center island, and it has a small set of rules that cover entering, circulating and leaving. You enter by slowing, yielding to every circulating lane, and yielding to crossing pedestrians. You travel counterclockwise around the island. Inside, you choose your lane by signs and arrows, you exit with a right turn, and you give trucks extra room for their wider arcs, without passing beside them. In this lesson we take those rules one at a time, and we end with a trap about who yields when you enter the circle.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Entering","fact_ids":["sec07-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Slow down.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09"]},{"text":"Yield to every circulating lane.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09"]},{"text":"Yield to crossing pedestrians.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Enter a roundabout by slowing down and yielding to every circulating lane. Then circle counterclockwise around the island, and yield to crossing pedestrians. Note the words every circulating lane. In a roundabout with more than one lane, you yield to traffic in all of them, not just the lane nearest to you. And the pedestrian yield from the intersection rules applies here too: pedestrians crossing at the roundabout are yielded to. The direction of travel is fixed: counterclockwise around the island. Entry is about patience: slow, yield to the circle and to pedestrians, then join.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Lanes, exits and trucks","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Pick lanes by signs and arrows.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"Exit with a right turn.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"Give trucks extra room; never pass beside them.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Inside a roundabout, pick your lane by the signs and arrows. Exit with a right turn. Give trucks extra room for their wider arcs, and do not pass beside them. Put as a contrast: cars hold tight signed lanes in roundabouts, while trucks swing wider arcs that forbid driving beside them. Because trucks swing wider arcs, the manual says not to pass beside them. Drop back and let the truck complete its arc. Your own lane choice comes from the signs and arrows before and inside the roundabout, and your exit is always a right turn out of the circle.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Entry yields to the circle","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Entering traffic yields.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},{"text":"Circulating traffic keeps moving.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},{"text":"Counterclockwise, signed lanes, right-turn exit.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap: some drivers think the cars already in the roundabout must make room for them as they enter. It is the other way around. Roundabout entry yields to every circulating lane, while circulating means counterclockwise travel, signed lane choice and a right-turn exit. The traffic in the circle has the right-of-way, and you join it only after yielding to every circulating lane. Once you are circulating, you keep to your signed lane, travel counterclockwise, and leave with a right turn. If an exam question asks who yields at a roundabout, the answer is the driver entering, to every circulating lane and to crossing pedestrians.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the truck","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two-lane roundabout.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"Large truck beside you.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"Drive beside it?","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: Noor drives into a two-lane roundabout and finds herself next to a large truck. Should she drive beside it around the circle? Work it out before reading on. The answer is no. Give trucks extra room for their wider arcs, and do not pass beside them. Cars hold tight signed lanes, while trucks swing wider arcs that forbid driving beside them. Noor should drop back and let the truck complete its turn, then continue in her own signed lane and exit with a right turn. The memory line for the whole roundabout is: yield in, circle counterclockwise, and exit right, with extra room for trucks.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Roundabout recap","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-R07","sec07-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Slow, yield to every circulating lane.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-R07","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"Counterclockwise around the island.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-R07","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"Signed lanes, right-turn exit, room for trucks.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-R07","sec07-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close the lesson: enter a roundabout by slowing, yielding to every circulating lane, and yielding to crossing pedestrians. Travel counterclockwise around the center island. Inside, pick your lane by signs and arrows, and exit with a right turn. Give trucks extra room for their wider arcs, and do not pass beside them.
